messages.subject: plot iccs
parts:
Hi Phil, I hope all is well. I'm sure this will go low on the priority list for mirt updates :) but I'm wondering if in the future there could be a plotting function added to mirt that would allow for users to plot the ICCs for particular response categories across multiple items for polytomous irt models (e.g., where you could plot the iccs for a grm model associated with responding in category 2 or higher across all items on one plot or faceted). The reason why this would be useful to integrate into the plot function is because I know you have the CEs built into that function, so it would be nice to leverage that (whereas creating the plots on your own, its a bit of a pain to then create the CEs). Again, i'm sure this low priority :) but could be useful. thanks!

Keri

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: plot iccs
parts:
Hi Keri,

Thinking about it having the argument facet_items = FALSE when type = 'trace' really should still create a set of faceted plots according to the category rather than previous default of including everything in a single plot (which was super messy looking). Here's what the new mirt output looks like (install from dev first):

library(mirt)
x <- mirt(Science, 1, SE=TRUE)
plot(x, type = 'trace', facet_items = FALSE)



Regarding the inclusion of CE for each response category, wouldn't that just make the plot look too messy to distinguish with all the shadings? There would be so much shade saturation that it likely would be difficult to see anything at all if the test has 5 or more items. 

Phil

parts:
Hi Phil, this is FABULOUS and beautiful-- THANK YOU!

You are right re: adding the CE functionality -- for long scales this would be a mess -- i work in the health outcomes measurement space so we often are dealing with short scales :) -- so thinking of it more from that perspective. The only other thought I had is that if you are using the ICCs in this format for determining cut-points, the CE could be useful just to visually understand the uncertainty associated with each ICC.

Thanks again!!! Super helpful.
Keri
